messages:
Alice: quick heads-up — new HF conversion (hf-lander/v2) failed our onboarding smoke tests
Ben: error logs or just quality drift?
Alice: both. streaming tests crashed and evals show significant token-level drift. I diffed the config.json and found a few surprising gaps after the HF->Redwood conversion.
Carol: list them?
Alice: 1) rope_scaling missing/null -> RW runtime expects an explicit rope_scaling object for some models. 2) sliding_window boolean mismatch vs chat template. 3) num_key_value_heads differs from our expected divisor of hidden heads -> KV cache reshape fails at runtime. 4) max_position_embeddings smaller than tokenized chat template length -> silent truncation.
Ben: can you paste the converted config snippet?
Alice: here:```json
{
  "model_type": "transformer",
  "hidden_size": 3072,
  "num_attention_heads": 48,
  "num_key_value_heads": 32,
  "max_position_embeddings": 2048,
  "rope_scaling": null,
  "sliding_window": false,
  "special_tokens_map": {"bos": "<s>", "eos": "</s>", "pad": "<pad>"}
}
```
Ben: okay, two immediate red flags: num_attention_heads (48) vs num_key_value_heads (32) -> mismatch unless HF uses head grouping. Our runtime requires num_key_value_heads to divide num_attention_heads or be 1-to-1 depending on config.
Darren: and sliding_window=false means our chat template padding will be applied differently. Redwood prefills prefix cache expecting sliding windows, so offsets shift when padding tokens are inserted — that explains token alignment drift in generation.
Carol: rope_scaling=null is dangerous; we have models that rely on linear/exponential rope scaling to match positional behaviours. If conversion leaves it null, runtime falls back to default which isn't always compatible.
Alice: repro stack: during warmup we get a reshape error: "KV cache shape mismatch: expected (layers, num_kv_heads, seq, head_dim) got (layers, num_attn_heads, seq, head_dim)". That crashes streaming path.
Ben: mitigation steps?
Alice: quick patch worked locally: set sliding_window:true, set rope_scaling:{"type":"linear","factor":1.0}, and align num_key_value_heads to 48 (or adapt runtime to accept grouped kv heads). Retested: streaming passes, eval perplexity dropped back in line.
Carol: did you try increasing max_position_embeddings?
Alice: yes, bump to 4096 for the template we use; previously the template with system + history + user exceeds 2048 after tokenization and gets silently truncated which reduced quality.
Darren: action items: (a) conversion script should fill in a sane default for rope_scaling when absent, (b) validate num_key_value_heads divisibility or transform into grouped heads notation, (c) warn/auto-adjust max_position_embeddings if tokenized template > declared value, (d) add a unit test for sliding_window vs chat template padding parity.
Ben: +1. Also add explicit check that special_tokens_map contains pad/bos/eos and that tokenizer mapping matches the chat template assumptions.
Alice: quant/regression notes: when sliding_window mismatch existed we saw +16% perplexity in our quantized fp16->int8 pipeline and embedding cosine similarity dropped ~0.04 on the eval set.
Carol: that magnitude is exactly the kind of regression we want to catch early. Put a regression alert on the onboarding job when those metrics exceed thresholds.
Darren: I'll open a conversion PR with heuristics and two new smoke tests (kv-reshape, padded-chat-length).
Alice: created issue #3421 with reproducer and logs: https://redwood/internal/issue/3421 (internal)
deploy-bot: opened PR 789 on origin/onboard-config-fixes with tests and a pending CI run
Ben: will review the PR. Please attach the minimal HF model tarball or a config-only repro so SRE can run locally.
Alice: uploading model tarball to the internal bucket now, sharing link in the issue. Running a full nightly eval tonight.
Carol: thanks team. small, tidy follow-ups will save us a bunch of flaky onboarding time. :thumbsup:
Darren: noted, I'll include conversion docs and a checklist for future onboards.
Alice: cool, ping me if the CI catches anything else.
